## b)  Data Pull


```{r}
# ---- Libraries ----
library(NHANES)  # for nhanes()
library(readr)   # for read_fwf, fwf_cols
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(forcats)

# ---- Config: cycles ----
cycle_years <- c(
  D = 2005,
  E = 2007,
  F = 2009,
  G = 2011,
  H = 2013,
  I = 2015,
  J = 2017
)

# ---- Variable map (correct file prefixes) ----
nhanes_var_map <- list(
  DEMO = list(
    survey.weight = "WTMEC2YR",
    psu           = "SDMVPSU",
    strata        = "SDMVSTRA",
    sex           = "RIAGENDR",
    age           = "RIDAGEYR",
    race          = "RIDRETH1",
    child_ed      = "DMDEDUC2",
    adult_ed      = "DMDEDUC3",
    marital       = "DMDMARTL",
    PIR           = "INDFMPIR"
  ),

  # Sleep: 2005–2014 (D–H): SLD010H; 2015–2018 (I–J): SLD012
  SLQ = list(
    duration_I_J = "SLD012",
    duration_D_H = "SLD010H"
  ),

  BMX = list(
    BMI = "BMXBMI"
  ),

  SMQ = list(
    smokes = "SMQ020"
  ),

  DBQ = list(
    diet = "DBQ700"
  ),

  MCQ = list(
    ever_asthma        = "MCQ010",
    active_asthma      = "MCQ035",
    cancer             = "MCQ220",
    emergency_asthma   = "MCQ050",
    # CVD conditions
    cvd_b              = "MCQ160B", # Congestive heart failure
    cvd_c              = "MCQ160C", # Coronary heart disease
    cvd_d              = "MCQ160D", # Angina pectoris
    cvd_e              = "MCQ160E", # Heart attack
    cvd_f              = "MCQ160F", # Stroke
    # COPD conditions
    copd_g             = "MCQ160G", # Chronic bronchitis
    copd_k             = "MCQ160K", # Emphysema
    copd_170k          = "MCQ170K"  # Alternative/supplemental COPD code
  ),

  # Depression (PHQ-9 items: DPQ010 through DPQ090)
  DPQ = list(
    DPQ010 = "DPQ010",
    DPQ020 = "DPQ020",
    DPQ030 = "DPQ030", # Sleep item
    DPQ040 = "DPQ040",
    DPQ050 = "DPQ050",
    DPQ060 = "DPQ060",
    DPQ070 = "DPQ070",
    DPQ080 = "DPQ080",
    DPQ090 = "DPQ090"
  ),

  # Physical activity: PAQ605 (E–J). For D we’ll use PAD200.
  PAQ = list(
    vigorous.work2_E_J = "PAQ605"
  ),

  PAD = list(
    vigorous.work1_D = "PAD200"
  ),

  # Household smoking: SMQFAM file
  SMQFAM = list(
    tobacco_1 = "SMD410",
    tobacco_2 = "SMD460"
  ),

  # Employment: OCQ file
  OCQ = list(
    ocd150 = "OCD150"
  )
)

# ---- Helper: fetch one NHANES file safely and select mapped vars ----
get_nhanes_data <- function(file_prefix, suffix, var_map) {
  file_name <- paste0(file_prefix, "_", suffix)

  dat <- tryCatch(
    nhanes(file_name, translated = FALSE),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(dat)) return(NULL)

  dat <- dat |> dplyr::rename_with(toupper)

  select_list <- setNames(
    c("SEQN", unlist(var_map)),
    c("SEQN", names(var_map))
  )

  select_list_filtered <- select_list[select_list %in% names(dat)]
  if (length(select_list_filtered) == 0L) return(NULL)

  dat |>
    dplyr::select(!!!select_list_filtered)
}

# ---- Core per-cycle builder ----
get_cycle <- function(suffix) {
  year <- cycle_years[[suffix]]
  message(sprintf("\n--- Processing cycle %s (%d-%d) ---", suffix, year, year + 1))

  mort_file <- paste0(
    "https://ftp.cdc.gov/pub/Health_Statistics/NCHS/datalinkage/linked_mortality/",
    "NHANES_", year, "_", year + 1, "_MORT_2019_PUBLIC.dat"
  )

  mortality <- tryCatch(
    readr::read_fwf(
      file = mort_file,
      col_types = "iiiiiiii",
      fwf_cols(
        SEQN     = c(1, 6),
        death    = c(16, 16),
        followup = c(43, 45)
      ),
      na = c("", ".")
    ),
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
  if (is.null(mortality)) return(NULL)

  demo   <- get_nhanes_data("DEMO",   suffix, nhanes_var_map$DEMO)
  if (is.null(demo)) return(NULL)

  slq    <- get_nhanes_data("SLQ",    suffix, nhanes_var_map$SLQ)
  bmx    <- get_nhanes_data("BMX",    suffix, nhanes_var_map$BMX)
  smq    <- get_nhanes_data("SMQ",    suffix, nhanes_var_map$SMQ)
  dbq    <- get_nhanes_data("DBQ",    suffix, nhanes_var_map$DBQ)
  mcq    <- get_nhanes_data("MCQ",    suffix, nhanes_var_map$MCQ)
  dpq    <- get_nhanes_data("DPQ",    suffix, nhanes_var_map$DPQ)

  pad    <- if (suffix == "D") {
    get_nhanes_data("PAD", suffix, nhanes_var_map$PAD)
  } else {
    NULL
  }

  paq    <- if (suffix != "D") {
    get_nhanes_data("PAQ", suffix, nhanes_var_map$PAQ)
  } else {
    NULL
  }

  smqfam <- get_nhanes_data("SMQFAM", suffix, nhanes_var_map$SMQFAM)
  ocq    <- get_nhanes_data("OCQ",    suffix, nhanes_var_map$OCQ)

  result <- mortality |>
    dplyr::left_join(demo, by = "SEQN")

  cols_to_pref_new <- c(
    "duration_I_J",
    "duration_D_H",
    "vigorous.work1_D",
    "vigorous.work2_E_J",
    "tobacco_1",
    "tobacco_2",
    "ocd150"
  )

  safe_join <- function(base, add) {
    if (is.null(add)) return(base)

    tmp <- base |>
      dplyr::left_join(add, by = "SEQN", suffix = c("", "_NEW"))

    for (col in cols_to_pref_new) {
      col_new <- paste0(col, "_NEW")
      if (col %in% names(tmp) && col_new %in% names(tmp)) {
        tmp <- tmp |>
          dplyr::mutate(
            !!col := dplyr::coalesce(.data[[col_new]], .data[[col]])
          ) |>
          dplyr::select(-dplyr::all_of(col_new))
      }
    }

    tmp |>
      dplyr::select(-dplyr::matches("_NEW$"))
  }

  for (df in list(slq, bmx, smq, dbq, mcq, dpq, pad, paq, smqfam, ocq)) {
    result <- safe_join(result, df)
  }

  for (nm in c(
    "tobacco_1", "tobacco_2",
    "duration_I_J", "duration_D_H",
    "vigorous.work1_D", "vigorous.work2_E_J",
    "ocd150"
  )) {
    if (!nm %in% names(result)) result[[nm]] <- NA_real_
  }

  result <- result |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      duration      = dplyr::coalesce(.data$duration_I_J, .data$duration_D_H),
      vigorous.work = dplyr::coalesce(.data$vigorous.work1_D, .data$vigorous.work2_E_J),
      employed      = dplyr::case_when(
        ocd150 %in% c(1, 2) ~ 1,
        ocd150 %in% c(3, 4) ~ 0,
        TRUE                ~ NA_real_
      ),
      cycle_year    = year
    ) |>
    dplyr::select(
      -dplyr::any_of(c(
        "duration_I_J", "duration_D_H",
        "vigorous.work1_D", "vigorous.work2_E_J",
        "ocd150"
      ))
    ) |>
    dplyr::distinct()

  return(result)
}

# ---- Execution: build nhanes.final ----
cycles <- names(cycle_years)
nhanes_list <- purrr::map(cycles, get_cycle)

nhanes.final <- nhanes_list |>
  purrr::keep(~ !is.null(.x)) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows()

# ---- Data Harmonization ----
n_cycles <- nhanes.final$cycle_year |> unique() |> length()

nhanes_cleaned <- nhanes.final |>
  mutate(
    # 0) Combined-cycle weight
    survey.weight = survey.weight / n_cycles,

    # 1) Race/Ethnicity
    race = dplyr::case_match(
      as.numeric(race),
      1 ~ "Mexican American",
      2 ~ "Other Hispanic",
      3 ~ "Non-Hispanic White",
      4 ~ "Non-Hispanic Black",
      5 ~ "Other Race - Including Multi-Racial",
      .default = NA_character_
    ),
    race = forcats::fct_collapse(
      factor(race),
      "Hispanic" = c("Mexican American", "Other Hispanic"),
      "Other"    = "Other Race - Including Multi-Racial"
    ),
    race = factor(
      race,
      levels = c("Hispanic","Non-Hispanic White","Non-Hispanic Black","Other")
    ),

    # 2) Physical Activity at work
    vigorous.work = dplyr::case_match(
      as.numeric(vigorous.work),
      1 ~ "Yes",
      2 ~ "No",
      3 ~ "Unable to do activity",
      7 ~ NA_character_,
      9 ~ NA_character_,
      .default = NA_character_
    ),
    vigorous.work = forcats::fct_collapse(
      factor(vigorous.work),
      "Yes" = "Yes",
      "No"  = c("No","Unable to do activity")
    ),
    vigorous.work = factor(vigorous.work, levels = c("Yes","No")),

    # 3) Household tobacco exposure
    tobacco_1_rec = dplyr::case_match(
      as.numeric(tobacco_1),
      1 ~ "Yes",
      2 ~ "No",
      7 ~ NA_character_,
      9 ~ NA_character_,
      .default = NA_character_
    ),
    tobacco_2_rec = dplyr::case_match(
      as.numeric(tobacco_2),
      0   ~ "No",
      1   ~ "Yes",
      2   ~ "Yes",
      3   ~ "Yes",
      777 ~ NA_character_,
      999 ~ NA_character_,
      .default = NA_character_
    ),
    tobacco_home = dplyr::coalesce(tobacco_1_rec, tobacco_2_rec),
    tobacco_home = factor(tobacco_home, levels = c("Yes","No")),

    smokers_in_home_460 = dplyr::case_when(
      as.numeric(tobacco_2) %in% c(0,1,2,3) ~ as.numeric(tobacco_2),
      as.numeric(tobacco_2) %in% c(777,999) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    smokers_in_home_410 = dplyr::case_when(
      as.numeric(tobacco_1) == 2 ~ 0,
      as.numeric(tobacco_1) == 1 ~ NA_real_,
      as.numeric(tobacco_1) %in% c(7,9) ~ NA_real_,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),
    smokers_in_home = dplyr::coalesce(smokers_in_home_460, smokers_in_home_410),

    tobacco_home_any = dplyr::case_when(
      tobacco_home == "Yes" ~ 1L,
      tobacco_home == "No"  ~ 0L,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    ),

    # 4) Education
    education.raw = dplyr::coalesce(
      as.numeric(child_ed),
      as.numeric(adult_ed)
    ),
    education = dplyr::case_match(
      education.raw,
      1 ~ "Less than 9th grade",
      2 ~ "9-11th grade",
      3 ~ "High school graduate/ GED",
      4 ~ "Some college or AA",
      5 ~ "College graduate or above",
      7 ~ NA_character_,
      9 ~ NA_character_,
      .default = NA_character_
    ),
    education = forcats::fct_collapse(
      factor(education),
      "Less than 9th grade"       = "Less than 9th grade",
      "Some high school"          = "9-11th grade",
      "High school graduate"      = "High school graduate/ GED",
      "Some post-secondary"       = "Some college or AA",
      "College graduate or above" = "College graduate or above"
    ),
    education = factor(
      education,
      levels = c(
        "Less than 9th grade",
        "Some high school",
        "High school graduate",
        "Some post-secondary",
        "College graduate or above"
      ),
      ordered = FALSE
    ),

    # 5) Marital status
    marital = dplyr::case_match(
      as.numeric(marital),
      1 ~ "Married",
      2 ~ "Widowed",
      3 ~ "Divorced",
      4 ~ "Separated",
      5 ~ "Never married",
      6 ~ "Living with partner",
      77 ~ NA_character_,
      99 ~ NA_character_,
      .default = NA_character_
    ),
    marital = forcats::fct_collapse(
      factor(marital),
      "Married/Living with partner" = c("Married","Living with partner"),
      "Single" = c("Widowed","Divorced","Separated","Never married")
    ),

    # 6) PIR categories
    PIR_cat = cut(
      as.numeric(PIR),
      breaks = c(-Inf, 1, 4, Inf),
      labels = c("Low","Middle","High"),
      right = FALSE,
      ordered_result = FALSE
    ),

    # 7) Sleep duration
    duration_clean = dplyr::na_if(as.numeric(duration), 77),
    duration_clean = dplyr::na_if(duration_clean, 99),
    duration_clean = ifelse(
      duration_clean < 0 | duration_clean > 24,
      NA,
      duration_clean
    ),
    duration_cat = cut(
      duration_clean,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 7, 9, Inf),
      labels = c("Short","Normal","Long"),
      right = FALSE
    ),
    duration = factor(
      duration_cat,
      levels = c("Short","Normal","Long"),
      ordered = FALSE
    ),

    # 8) BMI categories
    BMI_cat = cut(
      as.numeric(BMI),
      breaks = c(-Inf, 25, 30, Inf),
      labels = c("Underweight & Normal weight","Overweight","Obese"),
      right = FALSE,
      ordered_result = FALSE
    ),

    # 9) Smoking status
    smokes = dplyr::case_match(
      as.numeric(smokes),
      1 ~ 1,
      2 ~ 0,
      7 ~ NA_real_,
      9 ~ NA_real_,
      .default = NA_real_
    ),

    # 10) Diet quality
    diet = dplyr::case_match(
      as.numeric(diet),
      1 ~ "Poor",
      2 ~ "Fair",
      3 ~ "Good",
      4 ~ "Very good",
      5 ~ "Excellent",
      7 ~ NA_character_,
      9 ~ NA_character_,
      .default = NA_character_
    ),
    diet = factor(
      diet,
      levels = c("Poor","Fair","Good","Very good","Excellent"),
      ordered = FALSE
    ),

    # 11) Conditions (Asthma & Cancer)
    cancer = dplyr::case_match(
      as.numeric(cancer),
      1 ~ 1,
      2 ~ 0,
      7 ~ NA_real_,
      9 ~ NA_real_,
      .default = NA_real_
    ),
    ever_asthma = dplyr::case_match(
      as.numeric(ever_asthma),
      1 ~ 1,
      2 ~ 0,
      7 ~ NA_real_,
      9 ~ NA_real_,
      .default = NA_real_
    ),
    active_asthma = dplyr::case_match(
      as.numeric(active_asthma),
      1 ~ 1,
      2 ~ 0,
      7 ~ NA_real_,
      9 ~ NA_real_,
      .default = NA_real_
    ),
    emergency_asthma = dplyr::case_match(
      as.numeric(emergency_asthma),
      1 ~ 1,
      2 ~ 0,
      7 ~ NA_real_,
      9 ~ NA_real_,
      .default = NA_real_
    ),

    # 12) CVD Conditions & Composite
    across(all_of(c("cvd_b", "cvd_c", "cvd_d", "cvd_e", "cvd_f")), 
           ~ case_when(.x == 1 ~ 1, .x == 2 ~ 0, TRUE ~ NA_real_)),
    cvd = case_when(
      if_any(all_of(c("cvd_b", "cvd_c", "cvd_d", "cvd_e", "cvd_f")), ~ .x == 1) ~ 1,
      if_all(all_of(c("cvd_b", "cvd_c", "cvd_d", "cvd_e", "cvd_f")), ~ .x == 0) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # 13) COPD Indicator
    copd = case_when(
      copd_g == 1 | copd_170k == 1 ~ 1,
      copd_g == 2 & (copd_k == 2 | copd_170k == 2) ~ 0,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # 14) PHQ-9 Depression Screener Score & Items
    across(all_of(sprintf("DPQ%03d", seq(10, 90, 10))), ~ ifelse(.x %in% 0:3, .x, NA)),
    phq9 = rowSums(across(all_of(sprintf("DPQ%03d", seq(10, 90, 10)))), na.rm = FALSE),
    depress = ifelse(phq9 >= 10, 1, 0),
    phq_nosleep = phq9 - DPQ030,

    # 15) Logical consistency
    active_asthma = dplyr::if_else(
      ever_asthma == 0,
      0L,
      as.integer(active_asthma),
      missing = as.integer(active_asthma)
    ),
    emergency_asthma = dplyr::if_else(
      ever_asthma == 0,
      0L,
      as.integer(emergency_asthma),
      missing = as.integer(emergency_asthma)
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(
    -c(
      child_ed,
      adult_ed,
      education.raw,
      PIR,
      BMI,
      duration_clean,
      smokers_in_home_460,
      smokers_in_home_410,
      tobacco_1_rec,
      tobacco_2_rec
    )
  )

```

# Step 2:Constructing data analytic and building analytic figure


```{r}
library(dplyr)

# ---- Step 1: adults aged 18–79 ----
step1 <- nhanes_cleaned |> filter(age >= 20, age <= 79)
cat("Aged 18–79:", nrow(step1), "\n")                       # expect 39,248

# ---- Step 2: flag each exclusion (sequential, so each person is counted once) ----
has_elig <- "eligstat" %in% names(step1)

flow <- step1 |>
  mutate(
    excl_mort = is.na(death) | is.na(followup) |
                (if (has_elig) (is.na(eligstat) | eligstat != 1) else FALSE),
    excl_fu0  = !excl_mort & followup <= 0,
    excl_mec  = !excl_mort & !excl_fu0 &
                (is.na(survey.weight) | survey.weight <= 0),
    in_cohort = !excl_mort & !excl_fu0 & !excl_mec
  )

counts <- flow |>
  summarise(
    a_mortality_ineligible = sum(excl_mort),
    b_followup_zero        = sum(excl_fu0),
    c_no_MEC_exam          = sum(excl_mec),
    total_excluded         = sum(!in_cohort),
    primary_cohort         = sum(in_cohort),
    deaths_in_cohort       = sum(death[in_cohort] == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
print(t(counts))

cohort <- flow |> filter(in_cohort)

# ---- Step 3: active asthma in the primary cohort (observed; NA = imputed) ----
table(active_asthma = cohort$active_asthma, useNA = "ifany")

# ---- Step 4: complete-case subset (sensitivity analysis) ----
model_vars <- c("active_asthma","duration","sex","age","race","marital","smokes","diet",
                "cancer","employed","cycle_year","education","PIR_cat","BMI_cat",
                "vigorous.work")          # add "cvd","copd","phq9" if in final model

cc <- cohort[complete.cases(cohort[, model_vars]), ]
cat("\nComplete-case subset:", nrow(cc),
    "| missing >=1 covariate:", nrow(cohort) - nrow(cc),
    "| deaths:", sum(cc$death == 1), "\n")
table(cc_active_asthma = cc$active_asthma)

# ---- Step 5: reconcile with d.analytic (36,858 rows) ----
# Why were 39,248 - 36,858 = 2,390 people already left out of d.analytic?
dropped <- anti_join(step1, d.analytic, by = "SEQN")
cat("\nIn 20–79 but not in d.analytic:", nrow(dropped), "\n")
dropped |>
  summarise(
    missing_death      = sum(is.na(death)),
    missing_followup   = sum(is.na(followup)),
    followup_zero      = sum(followup <= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_asthma     = sum(is.na(active_asthma)),
    missing_sleep      = sum(is.na(duration))
  ) |> t() |> print()

# Zero-weight people still inside d.analytic (should be ~1,286)
cat("Zero/missing weight in d.analytic:",
    sum(is.na(d.analytic$survey.weight) | d.analytic$survey.weight == 0), "\n")
```

```{r}
library(DiagrammeR)

fig1 <- grViz('
digraph flow {
```

## c)Testing missingness/ MCAR test

```{r}

library(dplyr) # Required for if_else()

test_missingness <- function(d.analytic, vars) {
  
  # Create a working copy of the data frame to prevent contamination.
  working_data <- d.analytic 
  
  # --- MCAR Test ---
  mcar_result <- mcar_test(working_data[vars])
  print(mcar_result)
  
  if (mcar_result$p.value >= 0.05) {
    message("Data may be MCAR (p >= 0.05). No MAR models run.")
    
  } else {
    message("Warning: Data are NOT MCAR (p < 0.05). 
            Proceeding with MAR diagnostics.")
    
    # --- MAR Diagnostics ---
    for (v in vars) {
      
      # 1. Check if variable has missing data
      if (all(!is.na(working_data[[v]]))) { 
        cat("\n--- No missing values in", v, "---\n")
        next
      }
      
      cat("\n--- Running Missingness Model for", v, " ---\n")
      
      # 2. Prepare temporary data and missingness indicator
      temp_data <- working_data
      missing_var <- paste0("missing_", v)
      temp_data[[missing_var]] <- if_else(is.na(temp_data[[v]]), 1, 0)
      
      # 3. Define predictors
      predictors <- setdiff(vars, v) 
      
      # 4. Fit the model using tryCatch for robust error handling
      model <- tryCatch(
        expr = {
          glm(as.formula(paste(
            missing_var, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + ")
          )), family = binomial, data = temp_data) 
        },
        error = function(e) {
          cat("!!! ERROR: GLM failed for variable", v, ". Reason:", 
              e$message, "!!!\n")
          return(NULL) # Assign NULL to model if an error occurs
        }
      )
      
      # --- Guard Clause 1: Check if the model failed ---
      if (is.null(model)) {
        cat("!!! Skipping analysis and publish for", v, "due to model failure. 
            !!!\n")
        next
      }
      
      # 5. Check for significance and Guard Clause 2
      model_summary <- summary(model)
      
      # Check if the coefficients matrix is available and has predictors 
      ##(> 1 row)
      if (is.null(model_summary$coefficients) ||
          nrow(model_summary$coefficients) <= 1) {
        cat("!!! WARNING: Model for", v, 
            "produced no meaningful coefficients (e.g., only intercept or 
            singular matrix). Skipping significance check. !!!\n")
        
        # *** NEW: Robust publishing, even for failed models ***
        tryCatch({
          print(publish(model))
        }, error = function(e) {
          cat(paste0("!!! ERROR publishing model for ", v, ". Reason: ", 
                     e$message, " !!!\n"))
        })
        next
      }
      
      # Extract p-values (excluding the intercept, which is the first row)
      pvals <- model_summary$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"]
      
      if (any(pvals[-1] < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)) {
        cat("*** Note: Some predictors are SIGNIFICANT (p < 0.05).
            Missingness is likely MAR. ***\n")
      } else {
        cat("Note: No predictors are significant (p >= 0.05). 
            Missingness may still be MCAR within this model space.\n")
      }
      
      # 6. Publish/Print the result (print() ensures output is displayed)
      # *** NEW: Robust publishing for successful models ***
      tryCatch({
        print(publish(model))
      }, error = function(e) {
        cat(paste0("!!! ERROR publishing model for ", v, ". Reason: ", 
                   e$message, " !!!\n"))
      })
    }
  }
}
```

# Step 5. Multiple imputation

## a) Multiple imputation with MICE 


```{r}

 #First, we generate the nelsonaalen estimator, which synthesizes time-to-event 
# information based on followup time and event status.
 d.analytic$nelsonaalen <- nelsonaalen(d.analytic, followup, death)

 # Next, select the variables to be used as imputation predictors
 imp.predictors <-
 c(varset, # Predictors used in multivariable modeling
'nelsonaalen', 'death', # Outcome data
'survey.weight', 'psu', 'strata', # Survey design features (as auxiliaries)
'race') # Other auxiliary variables

```


## b) Configuring the Predictor Matrix and imputation methods

```{r}
# --- 1. Define Imputation Parameters ---
MAX_ITERATIONS <- 10


# First, we specify the imputation matrix
imp.matrix <- make.predictorMatrix(d.analytic)

## Here we override the default settings (THIS IS THE LOGICAL FLAW FROM CODE 1, but included for similarity)
imp.matrix[names(d.analytic), ] <- 0
imp.matrix[, names(d.analytic)] <- 0

## Here we manually specify which variables will undergo imputation and which
## variables will be used as imputation predictors
# NOTE: 'vars.with.missing' and 'imp.predictors' must be defined beforehand.
# Since Code 2 didn't define them, this assumes their existence.
imp.matrix[vars.with.missing, imp.predictors] <- 1

## Here we ensure that asthma variables aren't used to predict each other
vars.asthma <- c('ever_asthma', 'active_asthma', 'emergency_asthma')
imp.matrix['ever_asthma', vars.asthma] <- 0
imp.matrix['active_asthma', vars.asthma] <- 0
imp.matrix['emergency_asthma', vars.asthma] <- 0

## Here we ensure that a given variable is not used to impute itself
diag(imp.matrix) <- 0

# Second, we implement the MICE procedure
imputed_data<- mice(
  data = d.analytic,
  m = n.imputed.data,
  maxit = MAX_ITERATIONS,
  method = 'pmm',
  predictorMatrix = imp.matrix,
  seed = 123,
  printFlag = FALSE # Adopted from Code 1 to suppress output
)

print("--- MICE Imputation Complete ---")

# --- 4. Stack Imputed Eligible Data ---
impdata_eligible <- mice::complete(imputed_data, "long", include = FALSE)
impdata_eligible$ineligible <- 0


```

## d)Other steps after imputation
```{r}

library(dplyr)

# --- 5. Isolate and Replicate Ineligible Data ---
eligible_ids <-d.analytic$SEQN
dat_ineligible <- nhanes_cleaned %>% 
  filter(!SEQN %in% eligible_ids)
dat_ineligible$ineligible <- 1

dat_ineligible_stacked <- purrr::map_dfr(1:n.imputed.data, ~dat_ineligible %>% 
                                           mutate(.imp = .x))

# --- 6. Harmonize and Combine Datasets ---

library(dplyr)

dat_ineligible_stacked$nelson_aalen <- NA_real_

common_vars <- intersect(names(impdata_eligible), names(dat_ineligible_stacked))

impdata_eligible_final <- impdata_eligible %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(common_vars))

dat_ineligible_final <- dat_ineligible_stacked %>%
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(common_vars))

impdata_full_analysis <- bind_rows(impdata_eligible_final, dat_ineligible_final) %>%
  arrange(.imp, SEQN)


# --- 7. Filter out zero-time follow-ups ---
impdata_filtered <- impdata_full_analysis %>%
  filter(ineligible == 1 | (ineligible == 0 & followup > 0))

# --- 8. Define Cut-points and Split the ENTIRE stacked dataset ---
# We use the quantiles of event times from the eligible, non-imputed data
event_times <- d.analytic$followup[d.analytic$death == 1 & 
                                            d.analytic$followup > 0]
cuts <- quantile(event_times, probs = c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8), na.rm = TRUE)

impdata_full_split <- survSplit(Surv(followup, death) ~ ., 
                                data = impdata_filtered, 
                                cut = cuts,
                                episode = "tgroup",
                                id = "split_id") # Use a new ID name

print("--- survSplit() complete. ---")

# --- 9. Create your final pooled, split survey design object ---
allImputations_split <- imputationList(split(impdata_full_split, 
                                             impdata_full_split$.imp))

design_full_split <- svydesign(ids = ~psu,
                               strata = ~strata,
                               weights = ~survey.weight,
                               nest = TRUE,
                               data = allImputations_split)

# This is the final object you will pass to the PH test function
design_analytic_split <- subset(design_full_split, ineligible == 0)

print("--- Successfully created 'design_analytic_split' object ---")
```



# Step 6:Checking Proportional hazards assumption 


check the Proportional Hazards (PH) assumption
```{r}
library(survey)
library(survival)

library(survey)
library(survival)

# --- 1. Define your exact formula with tstart and followup (or tstop) ---
cox_formula <- Surv(followup, death) ~ active_asthma + sex + age + race + duration + 
               marital + smokes + diet + cancer + employed + 
               cycle_year + education + PIR_cat + BMI_cat + vigorous.work

# --- 2. Fit the model across all imputed datasets ---
fit_imputed <- with(design_analytic_split, svycoxph(cox_formula))

# --- 3. Run cox.zph() on a representative fit (e.g., first imputation) ---
# We fit a weighted standard coxph on the first imputation dataset for diagnostic visualization 
# because cox.zph() requires a standard survival fit object.
dat_1 <- subset(impdata_filtered, ineligible == 0 & .imp == 1) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(survey.weight) & survey.weight > 0)

# --- 4. Fit standard model with clean weights and check PH ---
standard_fit <- coxph(
  cox_formula, 
  data = dat_1, 
  weights = survey.weight
)

ph_test <- cox.zph(standard_fit)

# --- 4. View Results and Plot Schoenfeld Residuals ---
print(ph_test)

# Plot residuals over time (a non-zero slope indicates a PH violation)
plot(ph_test)


```
```{r}
library(survival)
library(dplyr)

cox_formula <- Surv(followup, death) ~ active_asthma + sex + age + race + duration +
  marital + smokes + diet + cancer + employed +
  cycle_year + education + PIR_cat + BMI_cat + vigorous.work

# Prepare one imputed dataset (Normal sleep as reference)
prep_imp <- function(imp_number) {
  impdata_filtered |>
    filter(.imp == imp_number, ineligible == 0, followup > 0,
           !is.na(survey.weight), survey.weight > 0) |>
    mutate(w_norm   = survey.weight / mean(survey.weight),
           duration = relevel(factor(duration), ref = "Normal"))
}

fit_imp <- function(d) {
  coxph(cox_formula, data = d, weights = w_norm,
        cluster = interaction(strata, psu), model = TRUE)
}

# ---- 1. PH tests: first imputation + robustness in imputations 2 and 3 ----
fits <- lapply(1:3, function(i) fit_imp(prep_imp(i)))

ph_test <- cox.zph(fits[[1]], transform = "km")   # one test per variable
print(ph_test)
print(cox.zph(fits[[2]], transform = "km")$table)
print(cox.zph(fits[[3]], transform = "km")$table)

# ---- 2. Publication figure: one panel per coefficient ----
fit1 <- fits[[1]]
zph1 <- cox.zph(fit1, transform = "km", terms = FALSE)
b1   <- coef(fit1)
print(names(b1))    # check coefficient names

vars   <- c("active_asthma", "durationShort", "durationLong")
titles <- c("Active asthma", "Short sleep (vs normal)", "Long sleep (vs normal)")

png("Supp_Fig_Schoenfeld.png", width = 12, height = 4, units = "in", res = 300)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
for (i in seq_along(vars)) {
  idx <- which(rownames(zph1$table) == vars[i])
  if (length(idx) != 1) { warning("Not found: ", vars[i]); next }
  plot(zph1[idx], resid = FALSE, se = TRUE, lwd = 2,
       main = sprintf("%s (p = %.2f)", titles[i], zph1$table[idx, "p"]),
       xlab = "Follow-up time (months)", ylab = "Estimated log hazard ratio, β(t)")
  abline(h = b1[vars[i]], col = "red", lty = 2)   # constant (PH) estimate
  abline(h = 0, col = "grey50", lty = 3)
}
dev.off()


```

## Testing additive interaction
```{r}

# Defining contrasts to pass to `svycontrast`
# NOTE: Suffixes .1 and .2 and .3 are used instead of .10 and .01 and .11.
#       However, a translation key is provided below
#
# r.1 == RR.1.0
# r.2 == RR.0.1
# r.3 == RR.1.1

## beta coefficients (from the regression model)
## beta coefficients (from the regression model)
b.list <- list(
  b.s.1 = "active_asthma",
  b.s.2 = "durationShort",
  b.s.3 = "`active_asthma:durationShort`",  # <- backticks
  b.l.1 = "active_asthma",
  b.l.2 = "durationLong",
  b.l.3 = "`active_asthma:durationLong`"    # <- backticks
)


## ratio coefficients (e.g., HRs)
r.list <-
  list(r.1.s = 'exp(b.s.1)',
       r.2.s = 'exp(b.s.2)',
       r.3.s = 'exp(b.s.1 + b.s.2 + b.s.3)',
       r.1.l = 'exp(b.l.1)',
       r.2.l = 'exp(b.l.2)',
       r.3.l = 'exp(b.l.1 + b.l.2 + b.l.3)')

## reri coefficients
reri.list <-
  list(reri.s = 'r.3.s - r.1.s - r.2.s + 1', 
       reri.l = 'r.3.l - r.1.l - r.2.l + 1')

## ap coefficients
ap.list <- list(ap.s = 'reri.s/r.3.s', ap.l = 'reri.l/r.3.l')

## si coefficients
si.list <- list(
  lnsi.s = 'log((r.3.s - 1)/((r.1.s - 1) + (r.2.s - 1)))',
  lnsi.l = 'log((r.3.l - 1)/((r.1.l - 1) + (r.2.l - 1)))'
)

# The estimation procedure
# NOTE: `survey::svycontrast` is used to implement the (non)linear combinations.
library(survey)
library(mitools)

res <- mi.list.of.svycoxph.models |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(b.list, str2expression)) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(r.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(reri.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(ap.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(si.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  mitools::MIcombine() |>
  summary(conf.int = TRUE)

res
exp(res[c("lnsi.s", "lnsi.l"), c("results", "(lower", "upper)")])   # S and its 95% CI


```

## i) Presenting the findings on forest plot

```{r}

library(tidyverse) # Includes ggplot2 and dplyr

# Create the data frame
hr_data <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Model, ~HR, ~Conf_low, ~Conf_high,
  "Crude", 1.63, 1.42, 1.87,
  "Adjusted", 1.38, 1.21, 1.57,
  "Short Sleep duration", 1.49, 1.21, 1.83,
  "Long Sleep duration", 1.47, 1.11, 1.93,
  "Normal sleep duration", 1.23, 0.99, 1.52
)

# Crucial step: Convert 'Model' to a factor and reverse the order
# This ensures they plot from top to bottom in the desired order
hr_data <- hr_data %>%
  mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = rev(c("Crude", "Adjusted", "Short Sleep duration", "Long Sleep duration", "Normal sleep duration"))))


forest_plot <- ggplot(hr_data, aes(y = Model, x = HR, xmin = Conf_low, xmax = Conf_high)) +
  
  # 1. Add the horizontal confidence interval lines (whiskers)
  geom_errorbarh(height = 0.1, linewidth = 0.8, color = "grey") +
  
  # 2. Add the point estimate (Hazard Ratio)
  geom_point(shape = 18, size = 4, color = "grey") +
  
  # 3. Add the vertical line at HR = 1 (the null line)
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # 4. Add the labels (HR and 95% CI) next to the points
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f (%s, %s)", HR, Conf_low, Conf_high)),
            x = max(hr_data$Conf_high) + 0.5, # Position the text far to the right
            hjust = 0, size = 3.5) +
  
  # 5. Set the X-axis to a log scale (common for ratio measures like HR)
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Hazard Ratio (95% Confidence Interval)",
```

## j)Kaplan_Meier plot by active asthma status

```{r}
############################################################
# Figure 3. Survey-weighted Kaplan–Meier curves by active asthma
#           with 95% confidence bands and numbers at risk
############################################################

library(survey)
library(survival)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)   # install.packages("patchwork") if needed

# ---- 1. Design: first imputed dataset, analytic cohort ----
# (Only 131 asthma values were imputed, so curves are virtually identical
#  across imputations; using the first imputation is standard for plotting.)
des1 <- design_analytic_main$designs[[1]]
des1 <- subset(des1, survey.weight > 0 & followup > 0)

# ---- 2. Weighted KM with robust (cluster) CIs ----
dat1 <- des1$variables
dat1$psu_id <- interaction(dat1$strata, dat1$psu)

km_fit <- survfit(Surv(followup, death) ~ active_asthma,
                  data      = dat1,
                  weights   = survey.weight,
                  cluster   = psu_id,      # robust variance clustered by PSU
                  conf.type = "log")       # CIs on the log scale

# ---- 3. Tidy data with 95% CI ----
grp <- rep(sub("active_asthma=", "", names(km_fit$strata)), km_fit$strata)

km_df <- tibble(
  time          = km_fit$time,
  surv          = km_fit$surv,
  lower         = km_fit$lower,
  upper         = km_fit$upper,
  active_asthma = grp
) |>
  group_by(active_asthma) |>
  group_modify(~ bind_rows(tibble(time = 0, surv = 1, lower = 1, upper = 1), .x)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(active_asthma = factor(active_asthma, levels = c("0", "1"),
                                labels = c("No", "Yes")))

# Helper: turn step data into ribbon polygons that follow the steps
step_ribbon <- function(d) {
  d <- arrange(d, time)
  n <- nrow(d)
  tibble(
    time  = c(d$time[1], rep(d$time[-1], each = 2)),
    lower = c(rep(d$lower[-n], each = 2), d$lower[n]),
    upper = c(rep(d$upper[-n], each = 2), d$upper[n])
  )
}

ribbon_df <- km_df |>
  group_by(active_asthma) |>
  group_modify(~ step_ribbon(.x)) |>
  ungroup()

# ---- 4. Numbers at risk (unweighted) ----
max_t   <- max(km_df$time)
t_break <- seq(0, floor(max_t / 24) * 24, by = 24)

risk_df <- expand.grid(time = t_break, grp = c(0, 1)) |>
  mutate(
    n_risk  = mapply(function(t, g) sum(dat1$followup >= t & dat1$active_asthma == g, na.rm = TRUE),
                     time, grp),
    n_event = mapply(function(t, g) sum(dat1$death == 1 & dat1$followup <= t &
                                          dat1$active_asthma == g, na.rm = TRUE),
                     time, grp),
    lab     = paste0(format(n_risk, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE),
                     " (", format(n_event, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), ")"),
    active_asthma = factor(grp, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
  )

# ---- 5. KM plot ----
p_km <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = ribbon_df,
              aes(x = time, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = active_asthma),
              alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_step(data = km_df,
            aes(x = time, y = surv, linetype = active_asthma),
            linewidth = 0.8, colour = "black") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "grey50", "Yes" = "grey30"), guide = "none") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("No" = "solid", "Yes" = "dashed")) +
  x_scale +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.75, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Months since interview", y = "Survival probability",
       linetype = "Active asthma") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.15, 0.25),
        legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.key.width = unit(1.2, "cm"))

# ---- 6. Risk table (no duplicate axis) ----
p_risk <- ggplot(risk_df, aes(x = time, y = active_asthma,
                              label = format(n_risk, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))) +
  geom_text(size = 3.3) +
  x_scale +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = c("Yes", "No")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, title = "Number at risk") +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  theme(axis.line = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"))

fig3 <- p_km / p_risk + plot_layout(heights = c(4, 1))
fig3

ggsave("Figure3_KM_asthma.png", fig3, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
ggsave("Figure3_KM_asthma.pdf", fig3, width = 8, height = 6)

```


## Black and white KM curves

```{r}

############################################################
# Figure 3. Survey-weighted Kaplan–Meier curves by active asthma
#           with 95% confidence bands and a risk table showing
#           At risk / Censored / Events for each group
############################################################

library(survey)
library(survival)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)   # install.packages("patchwork") if needed

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Data: first imputed dataset, analytic cohort
#    (only 131 asthma values were imputed, so curves are
#     virtually identical across imputations)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
des1 <- design_analytic_main$designs[[1]]
des1 <- subset(des1, survey.weight > 0 & followup > 0)

dat1 <- des1$variables
dat1$psu_id <- interaction(dat1$strata, dat1$psu)

grp_labels <- c("0" = "No active asthma", "1" = "Active asthma")

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Weighted KM with robust (PSU-clustered) 95% CIs
# ---------------------------------------------------------
km_fit <- survfit(Surv(followup, death) ~ active_asthma,
                  data      = dat1,
                  weights   = survey.weight,
                  cluster   = psu_id,
                  conf.type = "log")

grp <- rep(sub("active_asthma=", "", names(km_fit$strata)), km_fit$strata)

km_df <- tibble(
  time  = km_fit$time,
  surv  = km_fit$surv,
  lower = km_fit$lower,
  upper = km_fit$upper,
  grp   = grp
) |>
  group_by(grp) |>
  group_modify(~ bind_rows(tibble(time = 0, surv = 1, lower = 1, upper = 1), .x)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(group = factor(grp_labels[grp], levels = grp_labels))

# Ribbons that follow the steps
step_ribbon <- function(d) {
  d <- arrange(d, time)
  n <- nrow(d)
  tibble(
    time  = c(d$time[1], rep(d$time[-1], each = 2)),
    lower = c(rep(d$lower[-n], each = 2), d$lower[n]),
    upper = c(rep(d$upper[-n], each = 2), d$upper[n])
  )
}
ribbon_df <- km_df |>
  group_by(group) |>
  group_modify(~ step_ribbon(.x)) |>
  ungroup()

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Risk table: At risk / Censored / Events (unweighted)
#    At each time t: at risk + censored + events = group N
# ---------------------------------------------------------
max_t   <- max(km_df$time)
t_break <- seq(0, floor(max_t / 24) * 24, by = 24)

risk_long <- expand.grid(time = t_break, g = c(0, 1)) |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    `At risk`  = sum(dat1$active_asthma == g & dat1$followup >= time, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Censored` = sum(dat1$active_asthma == g & dat1$death == 0 & dat1$followup < time, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Events`   = sum(dat1$active_asthma == g & dat1$death == 1 & dat1$followup < time, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  pivot_longer(c(`At risk`, `Censored`, `Events`), names_to = "row", values_to = "n") |>
  mutate(
    group = factor(grp_labels[as.character(g)], levels = grp_labels),
    row   = factor(row, levels = c("Events", "Censored", "At risk"))   # top-to-bottom order
  )

# Check: last column should match total deaths in each group
risk_long |> filter(time == max(t_break), row == "Events") |> print()

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Shared x-axis
# ---------------------------------------------------------
x_scale <- scale_x_continuous(breaks = t_break, limits = c(0, max_t),
                              expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.02)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 5. KM plot
# ---------------------------------------------------------
p_km <- ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = ribbon_df,
              aes(x = time, ymin = lower, ymax = upper, fill = group),
              alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_step(data = km_df,
            aes(x = time, y = surv, colour = group, linetype = group),
            linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Black-and-white version: replace the two colour values with "black"
  # and the fill values with "grey50" / "grey30"
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("No active asthma" = "#E5736A", "Active asthma" = "#1BB6C1")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = c("No active asthma" = "#E5736A", "Active asthma" = "#1BB6C1")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("No active asthma" = "solid", "Active asthma" = "dashed")) +
  x_scale +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.75, 1)) +          # truncated y-axis; state in caption
  labs(x = "Months since interview", y = "Estimated survival",
       colour = NULL, fill = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.82, 0.88),
        legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.key.width  = unit(1.2, "cm"))

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Risk table panel (one block per group)
# ---------------------------------------------------------
p_risk <- ggplot(risk_long, aes(x = time, y = row,
                                label = format(n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))) +
  geom_text(size = 3.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, ncol = 1, strip.position = "top") +
  x_scale +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid       = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x      = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y      = element_text(face = "italic", hjust = 1, colour = "black"),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0, size = 11),
    panel.spacing    = unit(0.6, "lines")
  )

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Combine and save
# ---------------------------------------------------------
fig3 <- p_km / p_risk + plot_layout(heights = c(3, 2))
fig3

ggsave("Figure3_KM_asthma.png", fig3, width = 8, height = 8, dpi = 300)
ggsave("Figure3_KM_asthma.pdf", fig3, width = 8, height = 8)

```



## k) Checking for multicollinearity/ Active asthma
```{r}
# For survey models, wet need to fit a linear model to check VIF

library(car)

# Fit a linear model with the same predictors (using one imputation)

if("designs" %in% names(design_analytic_main)) {
  single_design <- design_analytic_main$designs[[1]]  #  using mitools
} else {
  single_design <- design_analytic_main  # it's a single svydesign object
}

# Fit a linear model to check VIF - FIXED SYNTAX
lm_for_vif <- svyglm(age ~ active_asthma + sex + marital + smokes + diet + 
                      cancer + employed + cycle_year + education + PIR_cat + BMI_cat + vigorous.work,
                    design = single_design) 

# Calculate VIF
vif_values <- vif(lm_for_vif)
print("Variance Inflation Factors:")
print(vif_values)

# Identify problematic VIF values (typically > 5 or > 10)
problematic_vif <- which(vif_values > 5)
if(length(problematic_vif) > 0) {
  print("Variables with VIF > 5:")
  print(vif_values[problematic_vif])
} else {
  print("No multicollinearity concerns based on VIF.")
}

```

## e) Forest plots for Hazards ratios for ever asthma

```{r}
library(tidyverse) # Includes ggplot2 and dplyr

# Create the data frame
hr_data <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Model, ~HR, ~Conf_low, ~Conf_high,
  "Crude", 1.18, 1.02, 1.38,
  "Adjusted", 1.17, 1.02, 1.35,
  "Short Sleep duration", 1.18, 0.96, 1.44,
  "Long Sleep duration", 1.44, 1.08, 1.93,
  "Normal sleep duration", 1.10, 0.89, 1.37
)

# Crucial step: Convert 'Model' to a factor and reverse the order
# This ensures they plot from top to bottom in the desired order
hr_data <- hr_data %>%
  mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = rev(c("Crude", "Adjusted", "Short Sleep duration", "Long Sleep duration", "Normal sleep duration"))))


forest_plot <- ggplot(hr_data, aes(y = Model, x = HR, xmin = Conf_low, xmax = Conf_high)) +
  
  # 1. Add the horizontal confidence interval lines (whiskers)
  geom_errorbarh(height = 0.1, linewidth = 0.8, color = "grey") +
  
  # 2. Add the point estimate (Hazard Ratio)
  geom_point(shape = 18, size = 4, color = "grey") +
  
  # 3. Add the vertical line at HR = 1 (the null line)
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # 4. Add the labels (HR and 95% CI) next to the points
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f (%s, %s)", HR, Conf_low, Conf_high)),
            x = max(hr_data$Conf_high) + 0.5, # Position the text far to the right
            hjust = 0, size = 3.5) +
  
  # 5. Set the X-axis to a log scale (common for ratio measures like HR)
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Hazard Ratio (95% Confidence Interval)",
    breaks = c(0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5),
    limits = c(0.8, max(hr_data$Conf_high) + 1.2) # Adjust limits to fit the CIs and the text
  ) +
  
  # 6. Customize Titles and Theme
  labs(
    y = "Model / Variable",
    title = "Forest Plot of Hazard Ratios/ever asthma"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), # Remove horizontal grid lines
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(), # Remove the Y-axis title (since model names are descriptive)
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.8, face = "bold"),
    plot.margin = unit(c(1, 4, 1, 1), "lines") # Increase right margin for the text labels
  )

# Print the plot
print(forest_plot)

```

# Step 12: Sensitivity Analysis : Complete case analysis

## a) Build  the design for complete case 


```{r}

library(dplyr)
library(survey)

# 1. List the variables that must be complete for your primary model
vars_for_model <- c(
  "death", "followup", "survey.weight", "psu", "strata",
  "sex", "age", "race", "marital", "smokes", "diet",
  "ever_asthma", "active_asthma", "emergency_asthma", "cancer",
  "vigorous.work", "employed", "cycle_year",
   "education", "PIR_cat", "duration", "BMI_cat"
)

# 2. Create complete-case analytic dataset
d_cc <- d.analytic %>%
  filter(if_all(all_of(vars_for_model), ~ !is.na(.)))

# Quick check of how many remain
nrow(d.analytic)
nrow(d_cc)

# 3. Define the survey design on the complete-case data
design_cc <- svydesign(
  ids     = ~psu,
  strata  = ~strata,
  weights = ~survey.weight,
  nest    = TRUE,
  data    = d_cc
)


```

# Step 13: Presenting all results into one single forest plot

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

# --- 1. Combined Data Setup ---

model_levels <- c("Crude", "Adjusted", "Short Sleep", "Long Sleep", "Normal sleep")

# Combine all data into one tibble (Using the group names provided by the user)
all_hr_data <- bind_rows(
  # Data for Active asthma (Primary model)
  tibble::tribble(~Model, ~HR, ~Conf_low, ~Conf_high, "Crude", 1.62, 1.44, 1.81, "Adjusted", 1.38, 1.23, 1.56, "Short Sleep", 1.50, 1.26, 1.79, "Long Sleep", 1.44, 1.06, 1.97, "Normal sleep", 1.23, 0.91, 1.32) %>% mutate(Group = "Active"),
  # Data for Ever asthma
  tibble::tribble(~Model, ~HR, ~Conf_low, ~Conf_high, "Crude", 1.17, 1.04, 1.31, "Adjusted", 1.17, 1.05, 1.31, "Short Sleep", 1.18, 0.98, 1.42, "Long Sleep", 1.41, 1.03, 1.92, "Normal sleep", 1.10, 0.88, 1.36) %>% mutate(Group = "Ever"),
  # Data for Emergency Hospitalization for Asthma
  tibble::tribble(~Model, ~HR, ~Conf_low, ~Conf_high, "Crude", 1.96, 1.40, 2.78, "Adjusted", 1.74, 1.26, 2.41, "Short Sleep", 1.85, 1.23, 2.80, "Long Sleep", 1.55, 0.75, 3.20, "Normal sleep", 1.63, 0.85, 3.16) %>% mutate(Group = "Emerg."),
  # Data for Age 18-65 model
  tibble::tribble(~Model, ~HR, ~Conf_low, ~Conf_high, "Crude", 1.91, 1.61, 2.26, "Adjusted", 1.39, 1.16, 1.67, "Short Sleep", 1.63, 1.30, 2.04, "Long Sleep", 1.40, 0.70, 2.79, "Normal sleep", 1.06, 0.76, 1.48) %>% mutate(Group = "18-65"),
  # Data for CCA model
  tibble::tribble(~Model, ~HR, ~Conf_low, ~Conf_high, "Crude", 1.53, 1.28, 1.83, "Adjusted", 1.27, 1.07, 1.52, "Short Sleep", 1.33, 1.02, 1.73, "Long Sleep", 1.42, 0.85, 2.38, "Normal sleep", 1.19, 0.85, 1.68) %>% mutate(Group = "CCA")
) %>%
  # Ensure Model is a factor with a specific order (for y-axis display)
  mutate(Model = factor(Model, levels = rev(model_levels)))


# Define custom color palette based on your previous non-CCA colors
color_palette <- c(
  "Active" = "#4CAF50",        # Primary model is green
  "Ever" = "#D946EF",        # Magenta / pink-purple
  "Emerg." = "#4169E1",       # royal blue type
  "18-65" = "#B49A2A",        # Mustard / yellow-brown / gold
  "CCA" = "#54C3E8"           # <--- NEW REQUESTED COLOR: grey20
)

# --- 2. Create the Cleaned Consolidated Forest Plot ---

# Calculate dynamic limits for text positioning
max_ci_val <- max(all_hr_data$Conf_high, na.rm = TRUE)
text_position_hr <- max_ci_val + 0.1 # Start HR/CI text slightly past the longest CI
x_axis_max_limit <- max_ci_val + 1.2 # Set plot area max to fit the text labels

forest_plot_combined_cleaned <- ggplot(all_hr_data, aes(y = Model, x = HR, xmin = Conf_low, xmax = Conf_high)) +

  # 1. Add the vertical line at HR = 1 (the null line)
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.8) +

  # 2. Add the horizontal confidence interval lines and point estimates
  geom_errorbarh(aes(color = Group), height = 0.1, linewidth = 0.8, position = position_dodge(width = 0.7)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = Group), shape = 18, size = 4, position = position_dodge(width = 0.7)) +

  # 3. Add the labels (HR and 95% CI) on the right
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)", HR, Conf_low, Conf_high), color = Group),
            x = text_position_hr, # Fixed x-position for HR(CI)
            hjust = 0, size = 3.5, family = "mono",
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
            # RE-ADDED BOLDING: Ensure the primary "Active" group text is bold
            fontface = ifelse(all_hr_data$Group == "Active", "bold", "plain")) +

  # 4. Apply the custom color scale
  scale_color_manual(name = "Models", 
                     values = color_palette,
                     breaks = names(color_palette)) +

  # 5. Set the X-axis scale
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Hazard Ratio (95% Confidence Interval)",
    breaks = c(0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0),
    limits = c(0.4, x_axis_max_limit),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0))
  ) +

  # 6. Customize Titles and Theme
  labs(
    y = NULL, # Remove Y-axis title
    title = "Consolidated Forest Plot of Hazard Ratios"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    # legend to the right of the plot area
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),

    # Fix to prevent the 'length 0' error
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),

    # Remove horizontal grid lines
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),

    # Set margins: (top, right, bottom, left)
    plot.margin = unit(c(0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5), "cm"),

    # Make Model labels bold
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10)
  )

# Print the plot
print(forest_plot_combined_cleaned)

# Save the plot
ggsave("forest_plot_custom_groups.png", plot = forest_plot_combined_cleaned, width = 14, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

## Testing additive interaction
```{r}

# Defining contrasts to pass to `svycontrast`
# NOTE: Suffixes .1 and .2 and .3 are used instead of .10 and .01 and .11.
#       However, a translation key is provided below
#
# r.1 == RR.1.0
# r.2 == RR.0.1
# r.3 == RR.1.1

## beta coefficients (from the regression model)
## beta coefficients (from the regression model)
b.list <- list(
  b.s.1 = "active_asthma",
  b.s.2 = "durationShort",
  b.s.3 = "`active_asthma:durationShort`",  # <- backticks
  b.l.1 = "active_asthma",
  b.l.2 = "durationLong",
  b.l.3 = "`active_asthma:durationLong`"    # <- backticks
)


## ratio coefficients (e.g., HRs)
r.list <-
  list(r.1.s = 'exp(b.s.1)',
       r.2.s = 'exp(b.s.2)',
       r.3.s = 'exp(b.s.1 + b.s.2 + b.s.3)',
       r.1.l = 'exp(b.l.1)',
       r.2.l = 'exp(b.l.2)',
       r.3.l = 'exp(b.l.1 + b.l.2 + b.l.3)')

## reri coefficients
reri.list <-
  list(reri.s = 'r.3.s - r.1.s - r.2.s + 1', 
       reri.l = 'r.3.l - r.1.l - r.2.l + 1')

## ap coefficients
ap.list <- list(ap.s = 'reri.s/r.3.s', ap.l = 'reri.l/r.3.l')

## si coefficients
si.list <- list(
  lnsi.s = 'log((r.3.s - 1)/((r.1.s - 1) + (r.2.s - 1)))',
  lnsi.l = 'log((r.3.l - 1)/((r.1.l - 1) + (r.2.l - 1)))'
)

# The estimation procedure
# NOTE: `survey::svycontrast` is used to implement the (non)linear combinations.
library(survey)
library(mitools)
library(survey)
library(mitools)

mi.list.of.svycoxph.models <- int_active_more     # <-- ADD THIS LINE

res <- mi.list.of.svycoxph.models |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(b.list, str2expression)) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(r.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(reri.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(ap.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(si.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  mitools::MIcombine() |>
  summary(conf.int = TRUE)

res
exp(res[c("lnsi.s", "lnsi.l"), c("results", "(lower", "upper)")])   # S and its 95% CI


```

# Step 16: Sensitivity analysis – excluding the first 2 years of follow-up


## a) Build  the design for complete case 


```{r}

## a) Build the design excluding the first 24 months

library(dplyr)
library(survey)
library(mitools)

# 1. Define the exclusion window (months)
lag_months <- 24

# 2. Create the lagged dataset (eligible participants with >= 24 months of follow-up)
#    Ineligible participants are kept so the design is complete; they are
#    removed with subset() below
impdata_lag <- impdata_filtered %>%
  mutate(lag_excluded = ineligible == 0 & followup < lag_months)

# Quick check of how many remain (first imputation)
impdata_lag %>%
  filter(.imp == 1, ineligible == 0, survey.weight > 0) %>%
  summarise(before        = n(),
            excluded      = sum(lag_excluded),
            remaining     = sum(!lag_excluded),
            deaths_excl   = sum(lag_excluded & death == 1),
            deaths_remain = sum(!lag_excluded & death == 1))

# 3. Define the survey design on the imputed data, then restrict
allImputations_lag <- imputationList(split(impdata_lag, impdata_lag$.imp))

design_lag <- svydesign(
  ids     = ~psu,
  strata  = ~strata,
  weights = ~survey.weight,
  nest    = TRUE,
  data    = allImputations_lag
)

design_lag_analytic <- subset(design_lag,
                              ineligible == 0 & survey.weight > 0 & !lag_excluded)


```

```{r}

                   svycoxph(Surv(followup, death) ~ active_asthma  ))

# Display the final, pooled results.

# Final Adjusted Cox Model Results (from Pooled Imputed Data)
summary(pooled_results, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)
```

```{r}
      cycle_year + education + PIR_cat + BMI_cat + vigorous.work

)


# Pool and check again
pooled_results <- pool(int_active_lag)
summary(pooled_results, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)


```







## h) Strata-Specific hazard ratios

```{r}

mod.1  <- with(design_analytic_main,
                            svycoxph(Surv(followup, death) ~ active_asthma * relevel(duration, ref = "Normal") + sex + age + race + 
                                       marital + smokes + diet + cancer + employed +
                                       cycle_year + education + PIR_cat + BMI_cat + vigorous.work ))

mod.2  <- with(design_analytic_main,
                            svycoxph(Surv(followup, death) ~ active_asthma * relevel(duration, ref = "Short") + sex + age + race + 
                                       marital + smokes + diet + cancer + employed +
                                       cycle_year + education + PIR_cat + BMI_cat + vigorous.work ))

mod.3  <- with(design_analytic_main,
                            svycoxph(Surv(followup, death) ~ active_asthma * relevel(duration, ref = "Long") + sex + age + race + 
                                       marital + smokes + diet + cancer + employed +
                                       cycle_year + education + PIR_cat + BMI_cat + vigorous.work))


# Pool the results from the list of model fits using Rubin's Rules.
pooled_results1 <- pool(mod.1)
pooled_results2 <- pool(mod.2)
pooled_results3 <- pool(mod.3)

# Final results
summary(pooled_results1, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)
summary(pooled_results2, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)
summary(pooled_results3, conf.int = TRUE, exponentiate = TRUE)


```


## Testing additive interaction
```{r}

# Defining contrasts to pass to `svycontrast`
# NOTE: Suffixes .1 and .2 and .3 are used instead of .10 and .01 and .11.
#       However, a translation key is provided below
#
# r.1 == RR.1.0
# r.2 == RR.0.1
# r.3 == RR.1.1

## beta coefficients (from the regression model)
## beta coefficients (from the regression model)
b.list <- list(
  b.s.1 = "active_asthma",
  b.s.2 = "durationShort",
  b.s.3 = "`active_asthma:durationShort`",  # <- backticks
  b.l.1 = "active_asthma",
  b.l.2 = "durationLong",
  b.l.3 = "`active_asthma:durationLong`"    # <- backticks
)


## ratio coefficients (e.g., HRs)
r.list <-
  list(r.1.s = 'exp(b.s.1)',
       r.2.s = 'exp(b.s.2)',
       r.3.s = 'exp(b.s.1 + b.s.2 + b.s.3)',
       r.1.l = 'exp(b.l.1)',
       r.2.l = 'exp(b.l.2)',
       r.3.l = 'exp(b.l.1 + b.l.2 + b.l.3)')

## reri coefficients
reri.list <-
  list(reri.s = 'r.3.s - r.1.s - r.2.s + 1', 
       reri.l = 'r.3.l - r.1.l - r.2.l + 1')

## ap coefficients
ap.list <- list(ap.s = 'reri.s/r.3.s', ap.l = 'reri.l/r.3.l')

## si coefficients
si.list <- list(
  lnsi.s = 'log((r.3.s - 1)/((r.1.s - 1) + (r.2.s - 1)))',
  lnsi.l = 'log((r.3.l - 1)/((r.1.l - 1) + (r.2.l - 1)))'
)

# The estimation procedure
# NOTE: `survey::svycontrast` is used to implement the (non)linear combinations.
library(survey)
library(mitools)
library(survey)
library(mitools)

mi.list.of.svycoxph.models <- int_active_lag     # <-- ADD THIS LINE

res <- mi.list.of.svycoxph.models |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(b.list, str2expression)) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(r.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(reri.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(ap.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  lapply(svycontrast, contrast = lapply(si.list, str2expression), add = TRUE) |>
  mitools::MIcombine() |>
  summary(conf.int = TRUE)

res
exp(res[c("lnsi.s", "lnsi.l"), c("results", "(lower", "upper)")])   # S and its 95% CI


```
